items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And having somebody with the stature of Etta wanting to be in the band was great.

ctx.x: Did it help to add the vocal element to your group from a working standpoint?

Yeah. Well I wanted to have a band with a singer. That was my dream. Because when I used to see the bands come to the south, the bands would always have a singer. So it helped a lot. And having somebody with the stature of Etta wanting to be in the band was great. So it worked out fine. It’s been a great help. It gives more balance for the presentation, so that’s really helped. I hope to bring the group up here some day.
To Hamilton? That sounds like a good idea.

items.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998
items.q: At first, when we first started working together I used to like maybe write a list you know. But after a while that just went to nothing and Houston started calling the songs

ctx.x: Those are the best kind, but not always, they don’t always happen. We were just talking, when you guys get your repertory together for certain kinds of gigs, do you each bring something to the table? You know, “I’d like to do this tune,” and work it out?

No. At first, when we first started working together I used to like maybe write a list you know. But after a while that just went to nothing and Houston started calling the songs, because I didn’t want to take my break to write lists to sing. And I couldn’t think of anything to sing. It got so — you forget what you actually — what songs you actually do. And he can call them in a minute.
I’m glad you said that. I have that same problem, remembering the songs that you know.

items.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995…
items.q: Houston has recorded numerous albums as a leader and enjoys a long time collaboration with singer Etta Jones.

ctx.x: Houston Person is a tenor saxophonist who is equally comfortable in a jazz quartet or with an organ based trio that leans towards R&B. Born in 1934, Houston grew up in South Carolina and was fortunate to play with future jazz greats Eddie Harris and Cedar Walton while in the military. He later attended the Hartt School of Music and toured with a number of organ trios. Houston has recorded numerous albums as a leader and enjoys a long time collaboration with singer Etta Jones.
Mr. Person was interviewed by Michael Woods and Monk Rowe on May 29,
